title: Common maize weevil in maize grain storage

Header: Common maize weevil in maize grain storage
Common maize weevil , Greater grain weevil , Maize grain weevil , Sitophilus zeamais Fubusi wa matindi in Swahili

Prevention: The weevils do not like hard kernel varieties, such as local hard dent varieties or
Harvest maize soon after it has reached maturity to reduce the chance of attack by maize weevils and other storage pests.
Remove and bury deep or burn infested maize residues after harvest.
Reduce infestation by cleaning all storage bins, containers, hats, bags from old grain rests and grain powders before re-filling.
Swept out powders and grain rests may be fed to livestock.
Store clean, very dry maize i.e. maize with 12-14% moisture content.
Preventively put botanical pesticide of pounded neem seeds (Neem cake) or fresh neem leaves in layers over grains (see direct control).
Monitoring: Regularly check stored grain every month.
Mainly look for the adult weevils and damaged grains with exit holes and feeding powder from grains.
Use sticky sheets within the storage structures to capture weevils
Once adult weevils or weevil feeding holes are seen, direct control measures should be considered immediately.
Direct Control: Remove adult weevils from the grains by sieving.
This is labour-intensive and cannot eradicate the weevils.
Mix thoroughly inert dusts such as ash and clay with the grains to kill the weevils through desiccation (200 g dusts with 100 kg grains).
Add pounded neem seed powder into grain storage at 20 g / kg maize grains.
Add fresh neem leaves in layers between piled maize bags
Contact research institutes for releasing natural enemies such as parasitoids (Anisopteromalus calandrae, Cephalonomia tarsalis, Lariophagus distinguendus,Theocolax elegans).
They need to be released early in the store.
Restrictions: Many storage pesticides are highly toxic and should not be used.
Fumigation cannot be done by untrained farmers.
Hire certified fumigators, but ensure that they are not using the most toxic pesticides.
Wear protective clothing and follow the instructions on the product label.
